name: Incident Reporting
summary: The lab reports serious safety incidents to governments within a set time, and publishes a summary.
description: Governments cannot respond to risks that they do not know about. Reports of incidents, such as a model that escapes its limits, show where safeguards fail.

criteria.label: To Government
criteria.description: The lab reports serious incidents to a government body.

criteria.label: Deadline
criteria.description: Reports go out within a set time, such as 15 days.

criteria.label: Public Summary
criteria.description: The lab publishes a summary of each serious incident.

criteria.label: Broad Scope
criteria.description: Reports include model misbehavior and loss of control, not only security breaches.

orgs.summary: OpenAI must report incidents to California and the EU. The Commission confirms some reports but says two were not filed. OpenAI publishes public incident reports.

events.title: Joins White House pledge to share risk information
events.summary: Signs the White House voluntary commitments, which include work toward sharing information with governments on safety risks and attempts to circumvent safeguards. They set no reporting deadline or format.

quote.text: Work toward information sharing among companies and governments regarding trust and safety risks, dangerous or emergent capabilities, and attempts to circumvent safeguards

events.title: California law requires 15-day incident reports
events.summary: SB 53 takes effect. Frontier developers must report critical safety incidents, including loss of control and deceptive subversion of controls, to the state emergency office within 15 days, or 24 hours if lives are at risk.

quote.text: If an incident is determined to be reportable, we will gather relevant information from the investigation and remediation phase for reporting to appropriate authorities within the required deadlines.

events.title: Commission confirms notice of Hugging Face incident
events.summary: A Commission spokesperson confirms that OpenAI notified the Commission of the Hugging Face incident, two days after its public disclosure. The Commission does not say what the notice contains.

quote.text: We are sharing preliminary findings at this stage to help defenders understand what happened and to help calibrate on what models are now capable of.

sources.title: Midday press briefing from 23/07/2026
OpenAI and Hugging Face partner to address security incident during model evaluation

events.title: Publishes full report on Hugging Face incident
events.summary: After its models escaped an isolated evaluation and compromised Hugging Face systems, it published a notice on July 21 and a full technical report on August 26. METR and Redwood Research published a review that OpenAI could redact.

quote.text: Today we are publishing our full technical incident report

sources.title: The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead
OpenAI and Hugging Face partner to address security incident during model evaluation
Brief independent investigation of agents’ behavior, reasoning and collaboration in the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident

events.title: Promises public reports on misalignment incidents
events.summary: Says it will publish qualifying misalignment cases, with an early notice for large investigations such as the Hugging Face incident. Says serious incidents should be shared with the US federal government.

quote.text: We also believe that serious safety, security and misalignment incidents should be shared with the US federal government, and we are working to propose reporting mechanisms.

sources.title: Our framework for reporting model misalignment

events.title: Commission says two incidents were not formally reported
events.summary: A Commission spokesperson says OpenAI filed no formal EU report on the RubyGems incident or the German wiki incident, both found by outside researchers. OpenAI says its RubyGems activity was benign.

quote.text: Based on our review, our agents used the RubyGems platform to access the internet to carry out benign tasks and retrieve public information

sources.title: EXCLUSIVE: OpenAI didn’t report safety incident under EU AI rules
AI safety incident reporting ‘not just a tick box’, warns EU
Researchers say OpenAI agents were behind May hacking campaign targeting RubyGems

events.title: Commission confirms reports but lacks full picture
events.summary: Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen says OpenAI and Anthropic filed incident reports, but the Commission lacks a complete picture and sometimes learns of incidents from the press. It sends both more questions.

events.title: Publishes account of three real-world evaluation incidents
events.summary: Describes three cases in which Claude models in a misconfigured third-party evaluation reached real systems. The next day, Commission officials said OpenAI and Anthropic had briefed them before going public.

quote.text: In a review of our cybersecurity evaluation transcripts, we found three incidents in which a Claude model reached the internet from within or while interacting with a third-party evaluation environment, and then gained unauthorized access to the real systems of three different organizations.

sources.title: Investigating three real-world incidents in our cybersecurity evaluations
EU in talks with OpenAI, Anthropic after rogue AI agent hacks

events.title: Risk Report describes safeguard incidents
events.summary: The August 2026 Risk Report describes several incidents, such as unauthorized access to a model through a vendor and safety classifiers that were not running. Some details are redacted.

quote.text: we believe transparency on this topic serves the broader safety ecosystem

sources.title: Redacted Risk Report, August 2026

events.title: Publishes alignment assessment and a fourth incident
events.summary: Finds biased reasoning and recklessness behind four incidents, including a January case found later, and releases a transcript. Signs an agreement for METR to investigate the incidents independently.

quote.text: We have signed an agreement with METR to conduct an independent investigation of these incidents.

sources.title: An alignment assessment of recent cybersecurity incidents

events.title: Reports minor unintended actions and briefs White House
events.summary: Describes lower-severity cases, such as a false police tip and forms sent on real websites, some run by government agencies. Says it briefed the White House, notified each agency and will keep reporting.

quote.text: We have briefed the White House on these cases and notified each agency involved.

sources.title: Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use

events.title: Framework adds incident response and reporting
events.summary: Framework 2.0 adds a global incident response program that reports critical incidents as appropriate. It names no authority or deadline. Version 2.1, published October 2026, keeps this text.

quote.text: We maintain a comprehensive global incident response program, including identifying incidents from both internal and external sources, and reporting critical incidents as appropriate.

sources.title: Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework, Version 2.1

events.title: Publishes account of Muse Spark evaluation incident
events.summary: Describes how a misconfigured third-party evaluation let a pre-release Muse Spark 1.1 exploit a real website. The evaluator, Irregular, found the issue and notified Meta and the affected party.

quote.text: Following that disclosure, we completed a detailed retrospective to understand the incident and its implications.

sources.title: Addressing an issue involving a third-party cyber evaluation of Muse Spark 1.1
